harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled systemd service on TCP 8080. The separate batchworker account has a persistent 128 MiB per-process virtual-memory limit. A failed 150 MiB batch allocation did not interrupt the API. Node1 was safely rebooted, its boot identity changed, and all required state recovered without changing the OS release or kernel.
actions_performed: Created separate inventory-api and batchworker accounts.
Installed a Python standard-library inventory API without adding or upgrading packages.
Enabled a hardened inventory-api systemd service bound to 0.0.0.0:8080.
Configured batchworker soft and hard RLIMIT_AS values to 131072 KiB through PAM limits.
Verified allocation failure isolation before and after reboot.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed service on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: systemd reports the service enabled and active under inventory-api; socket inspection shows Python listening on 0.0.0.0:8080; health and inventory endpoints respond successfully through node1's managed IP.

evidence.requirement: batchworker is limited to 128 MB virtual memory per process without interrupting the API
evidence.summary: Fresh batchworker sessions report soft and hard virtual-memory limits of 131072 KiB. A 150 MiB allocation fails with MemoryError, while API health succeeds immediately before and after.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Pre-change and post-reboot evidence both show Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 242af11e-49fb-4e07-a001-8016b2349acb; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; post-reboot boot ID changed to 61d73f52-30f2-48f2-b4fd-3e49a757940f. The enabled service, TCP listener, API data, health response, batchworker limit, and failure isolation all recovered.
